# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-11

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely good — I understand what Carnot does, I see `pip install carnot-ebm`, Apache 2.0, and a maintainer name within five seconds. But the moment I scroll into the evidence, trust drains: the same HumanEval benchmark shows three contradictory numbers (+3pp, +72pp, 0%→36%), several scores are suspiciously perfect (1.0, 60/60), one card brags that a 35B SOTA model scored 0% baseline, and the hero itself volunteers that the headline AUROC was "repinned from v2 0.9857." A skeptical stranger keeps the tab open for the pitch but starts doubting the numbers — which is fatal for a verification tool whose whole value proposition is trustworthy numbers.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Contradictory / implausible benchmark numbers — "Results" section (HumanEval appears as +3pp, 8%→80%, and 0%→36% on a SOTA 35B; "0.90 AUC vs 0.125 baseline"; perfect 1.0 and 60/60).
2. AUROC number-soup + a retraction note placed in the hero — "Recent progress" card ("0.9131 … architecture-only 0.8947 … Repinned from v2 0.9857"), four-plus different ~0.9 numbers across the page.
3. Pervasive insider jargon strangers can't decode — worst offenders: the "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" capability card, and version-numbered internal class names (HalluGuard v3, IterativeSelfRepair, EstimationVerifier, VeriCoT, CCTU, FoVer, PRM-BiasBench, paper-v6).

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- No single card breaks the hard word caps (longest bento body, "Why Energy-Based?", is ~77 words < 120; result cards are short < 60). Be honest: there is no hard-cap violation here.
- Soft bloat — cumulative density: Features (7 cards) immediately followed by Results (12 cards) = ~19 dense cards back-to-back. A stranger skims none of them. Results is under the 20-card cap but only just, and three of its cards re-measure HumanEval, padding the count without adding information.
- Nav bar — 12 text links + 2 buttons. Overcrowded for a landing page; on a 30-second skim the choice paralysis means none get clicked. Suggest trimming to ~5 (Get Started, Results, Quick Start, Paper, GitHub).
- "Seven capabilities" — only ~4 are actually verification capabilities; 3 are filler (see jargon/missing-fit below). The section is padded to hit a round "seven."

### Internal jargon
- "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" capability card — "scales Test-Time Compute (TTC) based on Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM) variance … intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning" — total opacity to a stranger; two undefined acronyms in two sentences, and it never says what I can *check* with it.
- Hero stat "382 Completed milestones" and "3,341 Experiment runs" — internal dev-process metrics presented as headline numbers. A stranger doesn't value "milestones"; it reads like project-management bookkeeping, not user benefit.
- "Recent progress" card — "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947", "Repinned from v2" — insider methodology terms in the most-read card on the page.
- Results cards — "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" ("publication gate" = internal process); "IterativeSelfRepair (HumanEval-50, execute-feedback-retry)"; "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC"; "VeriCoT equation-style CoT fix" ("CoT", "TP rate"); "HalluGuard v3"; "k=5 ensemble"; "PRM-BiasBench-style"; "CCTU constrained micro-benchmark" — class names, version numbers, and unexplained benchmark acronyms a stranger can't evaluate.
- Multi-step reasoning card — "AND-composed" — minor, jargon.
- APIs card — "VerdictRecord objects", "SessionMemory packs (export, import, diff, merge)", "MCP server" unexplained — code-level detail, not landing-page copy.
- Preprint section — "paper-v6" (internal version number) and "pending operator-initiated upload" ("operator" is insider; also tells the stranger the "Preprint" isn't actually on a preprint server).
- Blog cards — "arXiv:2601.18753 NTK" (NTK undefined), "Deep Think Rounds" — insider shorthand.

### Per-milestone narrative
- "Recent progress" hero card — "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit" reads like a changelog/retro entry, not landing copy. Honest, but it litigates an internal number revision in the first screen.
- Less egregious than classic milestone-narrative (no raw ".247"-style milestone IDs in prose), but the version suffixes ("v2", "v3", "paper-v6") carry the same commit-message smell.

### Inconsistencies
- HumanEval reported three ways: "+3.0 points" (Code result card) vs "8% → 80% (+72pp)" (IterativeSelfRepair card) vs "0% → 36%" (SOTA-35B card). To a stranger these flatly contradict each other; the differing setups aren't made legible.
- AUROC/AUC values scattered with no single source of truth: 0.9131, 0.8947, 0.9857 (all in one hero card), 0.91 (prompt-injection), 0.90 AUC (SVAMP), 0.125 (baseline). Two different "0.91" AUROCs for two different things invite conflation.
- "FoVer" is used both as the flagship benchmark (0.9131 AUROC headline) and as a weak strawman baseline (0.125) in the SVAMP card — same name, opposite roles, confusing.
- The arithmetic example renders three ways: "47 + 28 = 76" (hero, success card, code) but "47 + 28 = 7" in the "One-word-at-a-time" error card. A stranger reads "= 7" as a typo, not a mid-stream illustration.
- Meter-bar widths are arbitrary/misleading: "+3.0 points" → 14.6% bar but "+4.9 points" → 66.7% bar (no consistent scale); worst, "0.0pp accuracy delta" → a 95.6%-full green bar. The bars imply magnitudes the numbers don't support.
- Layout bug: the "Recent progress" `r-card` is nested *inside* `.stats-bar`, so a results paragraph renders jammed among the big stat numbers in the hero — looks broken/unfinished.

### Missing essentials
- Mostly covered, which is a real strength: one-sentence "what it does" ✓, install command ✓, license (badge + footer) ✓, maintainer named ✓.
- Weak spot — "why should I trust the numbers?" The section *claims* "every number is backed by a checked-in experiment artifact," but the numbers themselves (perfect scores, 0% SOTA baseline, below-random 0.125 baseline) undercut that claim rather than support it. There's no third-party/independent validation anchor a stranger can lean on.
- Single maintainer ("Ian Blenke") with no team/org signal may read as low bus-factor to an enterprise-minded stranger — not a defect, but worth noting.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — a perfect 1.0 with no sample size or credibility anchor.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100% on a small, self-described "PRM-BiasBench-*style*" (i.e., homemade) attack set.
- "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC — 0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" — a 0.125 baseline is *below random* (0.5) for AUC; a 7× lift over an anti-correlated baseline reads as a rigged comparison.
- "HumanEval pass@1: 0% → 36%" on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B — a 35B SOTA model scoring 0% baseline on HumanEval is not credible (these models score 70–90%); screams broken harness or cherry-picked subset, and 36% post-fix is still far below the model's known score.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" and "Ising sampler live on silicon" (100% bar) — clean/absolute phrasings with no error bars or artifact link inline.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero nails the job: plain-language value prop ("answers that sound right but aren't … the second pair of eyes"), the concrete 47+28 example, visible `pip install`, Apache 2.0, and a named maintainer — a stranger "gets it" in seconds.
- The "Extract → Check → Repair" how-it-works section and the Python quickstart are clear, honest, and well-scoped — they explain the mechanism without drowning in jargon. The "no fine-tuning, works with any LLM you can call" line is a strong selling point.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. Fix the evidence section first — it's the trust-killer. Collapse the three HumanEval cards into one with explicit setups, drop or heavily caveat the "0% → 36% SOTA-35B" card (the 0% baseline is not believable and reads as fabricated), and remove or re-frame the "0.90 vs 0.125 baseline" card (a below-random baseline looks rigged).
2. De-jargon the cards that strangers can't parse: rewrite or cut "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM"; strip internal class/version names (HalluGuard v3, IterativeSelfRepair, EstimationVerifier, VeriCoT, CCTU, PRM-BiasBench) from card titles; gloss FoVer/AUROC once in plain English.
3. Move the "Repinned from v2 0.9857 …" retraction out of the hero — keep one clean headline number (0.9131) in the hero; let the "Why We Report Two AUROCs" blog post carry the nuance.
4. Audit suspiciously-perfect numbers (1.0, 60/60, 100% bars) — either add a sample size + artifact link inline, or pull them; on a verification tool's page, perfect scores read as fabrication, not strength.
5. Fix the meter bars to a consistent scale (or remove them) — especially the "0.0pp delta" card showing a 95.6% green bar, which actively misleads.
6. Reconcile the "47 + 28 = 7" vs "= 76" example and fix the layout bug where the "Recent progress" card renders inside the stat row.
7. Re-scope "Seven capabilities" to the actual verification capabilities (Code, Maths, Typed constraints, Multi-step reasoning); relocate Research-ops / APIs / TTC-PREM out of "What you can check," and trim the 12-link nav to ~5.
